name: Validate and route authenticated order webhooks to a sub-workflow

parameters.content:
## Validate and route authenticated order webhooks to a sub-workflow

## Who's it for

Anyone who accepts webhooks from a payment provider, shop platform, or partner API and needs the endpoint to be safe to expose publicly.

## How it works

The webhook is protected with Header Auth, so a request without the shared secret is answered with 401 by n8n itself and never starts the workflow. Valid requests hit an IF node that checks the fields the rest of the flow depends on. Only complete payloads are handed to a separate processing sub-workflow, which keeps the webhook execution short so the provider does not time out. Each remaining branch ends in its own Respond to Webhook node, so the caller can tell a rejected payload (400) from a genuine success (200).

## How to set up

1. Create a **Header Auth** credential and set the header name and secret your provider will send.
2. Attach it to the webhook node.
3. Point the **Run order sub-workflow** node at your own processing workflow.
4. Edit the IF conditions to match the fields your payload actually contains.
5. Copy the production URL into your provider's webhook settings.

## Requirements

An n8n instance reachable from the internet, and a Header Auth credential. No paid service is needed.

## How to customize

Add conditions to the IF node for any field you must have. Swap the sub-workflow call for your own logic, or add a queue insert before it if you expect traffic spikes.

### 1. Authenticated entry point
The webhook uses **Header Auth**, so an unauthenticated call never reaches your logic. Point your provider at the production URL and send the shared secret in the agreed header.

### 2. Validate before you act
An IF node checks that the fields you depend on are actually present. A payload that changed shape upstream is rejected here instead of failing halfway through the sub-workflow.

### 3. Hand off the real work
The heavy processing lives in a separate workflow, so the webhook execution stays short and the provider does not time out waiting for it.

### 4. Answer with the right status
Both paths end in an explicit response, so the caller can tell a rejected payload (400) from a genuine success (200). A wrong or missing secret never gets this far - Header Auth answers 401 itself, before the workflow starts, which is why there is no 401 node here.
